lines.text: At dawn, the whole camp came out to watch the Warm One hunt.
I'll do it, my lord! My arm's nearly healed!
The guest hunts. Not his men. Not his dog.
I had never killed anything bigger than a spider. And I had apologised to the spider.
Elder Freydis, I can't hunt. But I didn't come with empty hands.
Tobin's stoves. Iron boxes with a heart of rimeglass, warm for a month without a single stick of wood.
Skeld do not trade. Skeld hunt. That is the law.
Then may I hear the law? The exact words?
A guest who would sit at our fire must first feed it.
Feed it. It doesn't say kill anything.
So I set a stove beside their fire, and lit its heart. Warmth rolled out over the camp like a summer morning.
That is not a hunt!
No. But it fed the fire.
And the Skeld laughed. Kell said nobody in that camp had laughed in a year.
The law is satisfied. I am not. Spend one night in the ice cave, Warm One, without fire. No one ever has, and lived.
So I spent the night in a cave of solid ice, with only my dog for company. For an hour, it was almost cosy.
Then a white wolf appeared at the mouth of the cave. Ash looked at her. He looked at me. He looked at her again.
Ash. Don't you dare.
He dared.
By morning, the ice cave was a pond, and I was sitting in the middle of it. Wet, alone, and perfectly warm.
The Skeld were waiting outside. So was a hunting party, just back from the north. Their leader had one eye, and red-brown hair going grey.
He wasn't looking at me. He was looking past me. At Wren.
...Father?
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter thirty-four, coming soon.
